title: Continuous CI performance regression detection: baseline fingerprinting, PR gating & significance testing
creator: Marco Santiago
description: Add a continuous performance-regression detection pipeline into CI that gates PRs when statistically significant regressions in tokens/sec or p95 latency are observed. Create per-model and per-workload baselines (golden runs) with fingerprinting and automated baseline updates. Integrate with GitHub Actions, store artifacts in the benchmark bucket, and post actionable PR comments with delta breakdowns and mitigation steps.
acceptance_criteria: CI workflow runs a deterministic benchmark harness on PRs touching runtime, scheduler, or model-serving code
Baseline dataset exists per-mode (chat, completion, embeddings) and per-sequence-length bucket with stable metrics: tokens/sec, p50, p95, tail
A significance test (bootstrap OR t-test with configured thresholds) flags regressions with false-positive rate <= 2%
PRs with >5% regression on p95 or >10% regression on tokens/sec are optionally blocked, configurable by repo label
Benchmark artifacts (raw samples, aggregated stats, plot images) are uploaded to gs://redwood-benchmarks/ci/ with retention policy
PR comment includes delta table, plot, baseline fingerprint, links to failing trace logs, and suggested mitigations (batching, kernel flags, quantization profile)
implementation_plan: Design: define canonical workloads, sequence length buckets, and sample sizes for stable p95 estimates
Harness: extend ci/bench/harness to produce per-request sample traces, token counts, latency histograms and tokens/sec
Baseline store: create baseline manifest with model-version, seed, machine-type, start-time and hashed fingerprint
Statistical test: implement bootstrap comparison with configurable alpha and minimum-effect-size thresholds
CI integration: add GitHub Actions workflow that runs quick smoke benchmarks for PRs and full nightly baselines
PR UX: implement GitHub bot that posts results, marks check as failed/pending, and links to artifacts
Rollout: start as advisory (non-blocking) for 2 weeks, then enable blocking for critical repos with opt-out label
metrics: false positive rate on staged PRs (%)
percent of PRs blocked by perf-check
p95 CI width after configured sample size
risks: Flaky benchmarks due to noisy infra leading to false positives
Too-small sample sizes causing unstable p95 estimates and developer frustration
Blocking PRs might slow down velocity if thresholds are too strict or not tuned per workload
Storage costs for retaining raw artifacts if retention policy not enforced
notes: Prefer bootstrap resampling for p95 comparisons because latency tails are non-normal
We should fingerprint baselines by (model, quantization, kernel-set, seq-bucket, machine-type) to avoid invalid comparisons
Quick smoke runs in PR must run within 6 minutes and use reduced sample sizes with conservative thresholds
Nightly full baseline job will re-run golden workloads with larger sample sizes to refresh baselines
Consider integrating with console regressions dashboard for long-term tracking and alerts
